classification.habitat: Tropical and subtropical plains, forests and riverine areas

identification.description: Large spiny deciduous tree with palmate leaves and conspicuous flowers; Mocharasa is the plant exudate.
identification.whole_plant: Large tree with a broad crown and often conspicuously spiny trunk when young.
identification.stem: Young trunk often bears conical prickles; mature bark becomes greyish.
identification.leaf: Palmately compound leaves with several lanceolate leaflets, often shed seasonally.
identification.flower: Large showy red to orange-red flowers appearing prominently on leafless branches.
identification.fruit: Large ovoid capsule containing numerous seeds embedded in silky floss.
identification.seed: Small blackish seeds surrounded by silky fibres.
identification.bark: Grey bark; exudate (Mocharasa) may emerge from wounded bark.

dosha.vata: not specifically documented in imported dataset

therapeutics.precautions: Use authenticated exudate; avoid assuming all Bombax products are equivalent.

major_constituents: Polysaccharide/gum fractions reported in exudate studies
phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Composition varies with source and processing.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Bombax ceiba is studied for phytochemical and traditional medicinal properties; evidence should be interpreted by plant part and preparation.
modern_information.safety_notes: Authenticate Mocharasa and distinguish it from other plant gums.
